name: planted facts: synthetic lectures with a hidden answer key
style: Every slide is static for its whole time on screen (no animation, no transitions): a white background; at the top the slide title in large bold dark-blue text, underlined by a thin blue horizontal rule across the slide; a bulleted list in dark grey with a round bullet before each item (left half when the slide has a chart, else full width); small grey slide number 'k / n' in the bottom-right corner. A chart sits on the right half: its title in dark text above the plot, blue vertical bars (bar chart) or a blue line with round markers (line chart), the value of every bar or point printed just above it, category labels along the horizontal axis, a horizontal-axis label, a vertical-axis label, vertical-axis tick numbers starting at 0, light grey horizontal grid lines, no legend. Nothing else is ever on screen: no people, photographs, icons, logos, drawings or other images. The narration is one off-screen lecturer (a synthetic voice); no speaker is ever visible.

rules.engine_blind: The pipeline is given video.mp4 only (file name video.mp4, no source URL, research off). Nothing in this file, the specs or the timelines reaches it.
rules.facts: Derived by fixed rules from each spec (suite_a.specs.derive_facts): a slide title, bullet, chart title or axis label is a visual fact when the slide's narration shares less than 0.5 of its content words and the whole narration never says it as a phrase; a spoken fact when the share is at least 0.6 or it is said as a phrase; neither in between (listed as partly_said, not scored). Every chart adds a chart_value fact for its highest value; a line chart also adds a chart_trend fact for the direction from its first to its last point unless the slide's narration uses a word of that direction (bar charts: categories, no trend). The narration never states a chart value (validated, digits and words). Every slide has at least 2 visual facts and one spoken bullet.
rules.published: A published cue is a standard cue (with a gap) whose status is verified, edited or approved, or an extended cue (no gap) whose status is extended, edited or approved. Held cues are not published and are not scored.
rules.overlap: Seconds during which a published standard cue's audio [start, start + audio_dur] overlaps a narration span (timeline.json speech), summed per video; must be 0. Extended cues pause the picture: counted instead is any extended cue whose freeze point lies strictly inside a narration span (must be 0).
rules.recall: Per visual fact, a judge (Nemotron 3 Ultra, temperature 0, JSON) names the published cues that convey it: the fact's specific content (the exact title or bullet wording up to paraphrase that keeps every idea; for a label, the label text; for a chart_value, the value with its category; for a chart_trend, the direction over the chart's span). A cue that only names the slide or the chart, without that content, does not convey it. Recall (standard) counts standard cues only; recall (with extended) counts standard and extended cues. Also reported: timely recall (a conveying cue starts while that slide is on screen) and recall by fact kind.
rules.exact_match: Deterministic, no model: a title fact matches when one published cue contains the slide title as a whole-token phrase after normalisation (lower case, punctuation and spacing ignored); a chart_value fact matches when one published cue states the value (digits with optional thousands commas, or English number words) and contains its category label as a phrase. Reported separately for standard and with extended.
rules.hallucination: Per claim of a published cue (the claims in the run's cues.json), the judge decides supported or unsupported by this key: the slide inventory (exact on-screen text, chart data, ticks and the fixed style), the slide time ranges and the narration. Text quoted or read from the screen must match exactly; a number must match the chart or the slide; anything not established by the key (an object, a colour, a person, an image, a value, a relation) is unsupported. Rate = unsupported claims / claims. Also reported per cue (a cue with any unsupported claim).
rules.decoys: Per absent decoy, the judge names the published cues that state it or something it asserts; expected 0. Deterministic check: a number written in digits in a decoy (and nowhere in the video) appearing in a published cue.
rules.redundancy: Per published cue, the judge decides whether it restates a spoken fact or anything the narration says (adding nothing visual). Rate = such cues / published cues; also the share of spoken facts restated by any cue.
rules.cost_and_speed: Ledger spend of each run's run id (model calls and Tavily separately) per minute of video; processing seconds (wall clock of lull.pipeline.run) per minute of video; verified, held and extended counts from the run's manifest.
rules.aggregation: Pooled over the twelve videos (sum of numerators / sum of denominators). 95% intervals: percentile bootstrap over videos, 10000 resamples, seed 20261028.
rules.judge: nvidia/Nemotron-3-Ultra-550b-a55b on Nebius Token Factory, temperature 0, reasoning on, strict JSON schema. Two calls per video: (1) coverage: for every visual fact, spoken fact and absent decoy, the ids of the published cues that convey it; (2) claims: every claim of every published cue supported or unsupported, and every published cue restates the narration or not. The judge sees this key's entry for the video and the published cues (id, track, start time, text, claim texts), never the engine's own verdicts. One run per video; no re-judging to change a result.
rules.judge_probe: A check of the judge itself on videos a01, a05 and a09: synthetic cues made from the key (one per visual fact, its text; one per decoy, its text) are judged the same way. Reported: share of facts the judge credits to their own probe cue, share of decoys it credits to their probe cue, share of fact-cue claims judged supported and of decoy-cue claims judged unsupported.

narration.text: Energy exists in multiple identifiable forms across the universe.
These distinct forms allow energy to transform and transfer.
Work occurs when force gets applied over a distance.
This mechanical action transfers energy between objects.
The First law governs energy conservation in all processes.
This fundamental principle ensures energy remains constant.
